note: Holdings-relevant market news, researched daily by the intel agent (multi-theme sweep: precious metals, HK tech, SGX/Singapore, rare earths, macro) with sources. The "actionable" line relates each item to this specific portfolio. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Gold steadies near $4,150 as markets await June FOMC minutes and the July 14 CPI print; July hold priced at ~76-84%
items.summary: Gold held around $4,150/oz Tuesday after a volatile start to the week, with traders awaiting the minutes of the Fed's June meeting (Warsh's first, where rates were held at 3.50%-3.75% with a hawkish dot plot) plus services PMI, ADP and jobless claims data this week. CME FedWatch showed roughly 75.6% hold probability for the July 28-29 meeting as of July 4, with other trackers near 84% hold / 15% for a 25bp hike; June CPI lands July 14 and is the key catalyst between now and the meeting. With inflation still running near 4%, the hike-by-year-end debate (about two-thirds priced) remains the dominant swing factor for precious metals.
items.actionable: Mark July 14 (June CPI) and July 29 (FOMC) as the two binary risk dates for the levered silver position — consider pre-positioning stops or option protection before CPI rather than after, since June proved how fast hike repricing hits silver.

items.headline: DBS trades at record ~S$67 ahead of 6 August results; consensus target sits slightly below spot
items.summary: DBS shares traded around S$66.9-67.7 on 7 July 2026 (up ~1.1% on the day), pushing through the prior S$67.00 52-week high after closing S$66.68 on 3 July. Consensus 12-month price target of ~S$65.68 implies roughly 2% downside from spot, with the stock at a rich ~2.2x book value. Recent results were strong (3Q25 record total income S$5.93bn, +3% y/y; wealth-management fees S$1.58bn, +20% y/y), but with SORA/rates easing, NIM pressure is the key question into the 6 August 2026 earnings report.
items.actionable: Hold D05.SI for dividend support but do not add at ~2.2x book before the 6 August results; consider trimming into strength or rotating the increment into S-REITs, which benefit from the same falling-rate dynamic that squeezes DBS's NIM.

items.headline: Silver rebounds to $61-63 with a ~6% weekly gain — best week in 5+ weeks; SILJ +3.2% and GDX +4.5% on July 3
items.summary: Silver rose above $62/oz late last week, its highest since June 23, logging a nearly 6% weekly gain (Forbes had spot at $62.32 on July 3, +5.25% w/w) as the weak jobs data dampened hike expectations; September futures opened Monday July 6 at $62.92, about 3% above Friday's $61.06 close. Gold broke back above $4,100 after the jobs report and steadied near $4,150. Miner ETFs participated strongly: on July 3, SILJ traded up 3.16% to $26.73 (range $26.19-$27.50) and GDX rose 4.48% to $78.43 — leveraged confirmation of the metal's bounce.
items.actionable: Your SILJ/SLVP/GDX sleeve is doing its job as high-beta exposure to the bounce — if you want to reduce total portfolio leverage, trimming the levered 1,777oz silver position into this strength while keeping the miner ETFs preserves upside with less liquidation risk.

items.headline: 3M SORA holds near ~1.09% into July as analysts eye a slight S$NEER band steepening at MAS's late-July meeting
items.summary: Compounded 3-month SORA sits around 1.09% in early July 2026 (vs ~1.08% in June), roughly 115bps below 2024-25 levels and near pre-2022-hike lows - a direct funding-cost tailwind for S-REIT refinancing (DBS research estimates up to ~200bps savings on 2026-27 refinancings). On policy, MAS already steepened the S$NEER appreciation path to ~1%/yr from 0.5% in April 2026 on higher inflation forecasts (core/headline raised to 1.5-2.5%), and a 24 June analyst note argues MAS may slightly steepen the band again in July - though with SGD already near the top of the band (USD/SGD within ~0.45% of the implied strong edge, ~1.28-1.30 zone), further SGD upside looks capped.
items.actionable: Tilt incremental SGD allocation toward S-REITs over banks ahead of the late-July MAS statement - low SORA compresses REIT funding costs and squeezes bank margins; avoid paying up for further SGD appreciation given band-top constraints.

items.headline: Brent slides below $71-72, down ~38% from the $126 war peak, as US-Iran interim peace holds and Hormuz traffic recovers; OPEC+ lifts quotas
items.summary: Oil fell to levels last seen before the US-Israel war on Iran began: Brent dipped below $71 (later ~$72, WTI ~$69) — down more than 38% from the April 30 post-war peak above $126 — after Qatar-mediated Doha talks produced 'positive progress' on the US-Iran memorandum of understanding and Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic continued recovering. The curve has flipped from backwardation to contango and OPEC+ agreed to raise next month's production quotas, though talks remain stalled on freedom-of-navigation terms, keeping headline risk alive. Falling oil is disinflationary — easing pressure on Warsh's Fed to hike — but it also drains the geopolitical safe-haven bid that had supported gold and silver.
items.actionable: Don't count on an Iran-risk premium to rescue silver — the bull case from here rests on cooling US data and fading hike odds, so watch Hormuz/freedom-of-navigation headlines mainly as a two-way volatility source.

items.headline: Tencent buys back 1.1 million shares for HK$500.9 million on July 3 as daily repurchase programme continues
items.summary: An HKEX filing shows Tencent repurchased about 1.1 million shares for HK$500.9 million on 3 July 2026 (implied average ~HK$455/share), per Reuters. Tencent's investor relations page also shows a Next Day Disclosure Return on changes in issued shares and buybacks dated 6 July 2026, confirming the daily buyback cadence continued into early July despite broad Hang Seng weakness.
items.actionable: Hold 0700.HK; the persistent buyback bid around HK$450-460 offers downside support - consider adding on dips into that zone rather than chasing rallies.

items.headline: Mainland investors bought net HK$27.1bn of HK stocks in June, favouring SMIC and Zhipu AI, even as Hang Seng fell 9.1%
items.summary: SCMP (3 July 2026): southbound Stock Connect net buying reached HK$27.1bn (US$3.5bn) in June, reversing May's HK$3.6bn outflow, with mainland investors dip-buying AI plays led by SMIC and Zhipu AI (Kingboard was the single largest beneficiary at ~HK$20bn). H1 2026 southbound inflows totalled HK$305.5bn, down ~60% y/y. The HSI fell 9.1% in June - its biggest monthly drop in more than two years - and Hong Kong ended H1 2026 down ~11%, among the world's worst-performing markets; analysts see upside if Fed rate-cut expectations revive given depressed valuations.
items.actionable: Maintain 0981.HK exposure - it is a preferred southbound AI/semi vehicle - but size positions for volatility (stock traded HK$72.50-80.50 intraday recently vs a HK$93.50 52-week high); a Fed-cut repricing is the main index-level upside trigger.

items.headline: June payrolls miss badly at +57,000 (consensus 115,000) with -74,000 in revisions; near-term Fed hike odds crumble
items.summary: Nonfarm payrolls rose just 57,000 in June — the weakest in four months and roughly half the Dow Jones consensus of 115,000 — while April/May were revised down by a combined 74,000. The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.2%, but only because labor-force participation fell 0.3pt to 61.5%, the lowest since March 2021. Traders scaled back tightening bets sharply: September hike odds fell to roughly 50% from about two-thirds pre-report, effectively taking September off the table for many, with October remaining a residual possibility.
items.actionable: The soft labor print is the single most metal-friendly data point of the week — it directly reduces the hike-repricing risk that crushed your silver stack in June, so it argues for holding rather than de-risking into strength.

items.headline: Xiaomi shares jump ~5% after June EV deliveries top 30,000 for a third straight month; H1 at ~33% of 550k target
items.summary: CNBC reported on 2 July 2026 that Hong Kong-listed Xiaomi climbed about 5% (BYD ~9%) after June delivery figures: Xiaomi exceeded 30,000 EV deliveries for a third consecutive month, with January-June shipments of roughly 180,000 units - about 33% of its 550,000-unit 2026 target, per Citi. Citi flagged the August launch of the YU9 luxury SUV as the next catalyst. The EV unit remains loss-making (Q1 2026 operating loss ~RMB3.1bn) amid China's price war.
items.actionable: Hold 1810.HK; monthly delivery prints and the August YU9 launch are the key catalysts - wait for evidence of a H2 volume ramp before adding, as the FY target needs ~370k deliveries in H2.

items.headline: Silver's June crash confirmed as worst month since 2011: SLV -20%+, silver roughly halved from January's ~$120 peak to ~$58-60
items.summary: Benzinga (July 1) tallied the damage: silver fell more than 20% in June — its worst month since September 2011 — leaving it near $60/oz versus a late-January peak around $120, while gold slid over 11% in June and sits ~30% below its early-2026 high. The rout was driven by new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh crystallizing rate-HIKE expectations (futures at the time priced an October hike as near-certain, with roughly even odds of a second by March 2027) and a 2.4% June surge in the dollar index. A separate Rio Times piece (July 2) notes analysts are split on whether the low is in, with silver down 51% from peak; some banks still see this as 'a pause rather than a turn.'
items.actionable: With a 1,777oz levered silver position that just took a ~50% peak-to-trough underlying drawdown, size your remaining leverage so a retest of the June low (~$58 or below) cannot force liquidation, because credible analysts still call the bottom unconfirmed.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh at Sintra: inflation 'too high' (headline PCE 4.1%, core 3.4% in May) but declines to guide on July hike
items.summary: Speaking at the ECB's Sintra forum on July 1, Kevin Warsh said the Fed 'will not be comfortable' with inflation above 2% and will 'deliver price stability,' while noting inflation risks and expectations have recently come down; he refused forward guidance ahead of the July 28-29 FOMC. The Fed's preferred gauge showed core inflation at 3.4% and headline at 4.1% in May — the backdrop for the June dot plot in which 9 of 19 officials projected a hike by end-2026. Markets currently price roughly 76-84% odds of a hold at the July meeting (funds rate 3.50%-3.75%), but still embed about two-thirds odds of at least one hike by December.
items.actionable: Treat the July 29 FOMC as a likely hold but keep hedges through the June CPI print on July 14 — a hot number would revive the hike pricing that caused June's metals crash.

items.headline: Frasers Centrepoint Trust to divest White Sands mall for S$467m - 8.4% above valuation - cutting gearing to 36.5%
items.summary: FCT announced on 30 June 2026 a put-and-call option agreement to sell White Sands (Pasir Ris) to Growth Capital Pte Ltd for S$467.0m, 8.4% above its S$431.0m independent valuation as at 31 May 2026, crystallising an estimated ~S$32.4m net gain. Proceeds will mainly repay debt, lowering aggregate leverage from 40.0% to 36.5% and rebuilding acquisition headroom; completion is expected around 30 September 2026. Pro-forma DPU dips slightly ex-asset.
items.actionable: Hold/add retail S-REITs incl. FCT - premium-to-valuation divestments plus de-gearing to 36.5% validate NAVs and set up accretive redeployment as SORA falls; watch for FCT's reinvestment announcement.

items.headline: Pentagon inks $1.2 billion in rare-earth loans — $725M to Energy Fuels, $500M to Phoenix Tailings — as UUUU also buys magnet maker VAC for $1.9B
items.summary: The DoD Office of Strategic Capital signed a $725 million, 20-year conditional loan commitment with Energy Fuels on June 18 to expand rare-earth processing at White Mesa Mill (UUUU rallied ~9%), days after a $500 million conditional loan to Phoenix Tailings for a separation and metallization plant targeting 2028 operations. On June 23 Energy Fuels separately agreed to acquire German magnet maker Vacuumschmelze for ~$1.9 billion ($718M cash plus 65.85M new shares, closing early 2027), which would make it the first Western company integrated from mining to finished NdFeB magnets.
items.actionable: Washington is putting a financing floor under Western rare-earth economics, so a starter position in UUUU or MP funded from cash is reasonable — but note UUUU's large VAC share issuance creates a dilution/integration overhang worth letting settle first.

items.headline: China blacklists MP Materials and USA Rare Earth among 10 US firms, then adds whistleblower hotline to tighten export enforcement
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce added 10 US companies — including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth plus defense firms — to its export control list effective June 22, barring Chinese exporters and third-party re-exporters from supplying them with dual-use items, in retaliation for the Pentagon's expansion of its Chinese Military Companies list; MP fell 13.4% over June. On June 24 MOFCOM also launched a whistleblower hotline (effective July 1) rewarding tips on unauthorized strategic-mineral exports and transshipment, signaling aggressive enforcement of the export-control regime.
items.actionable: Escalating Chinese restrictions raise the scarcity premium on ex-China supply and validate the Western onshoring thesis, so treat MP/USAR headline dips as potential scale-in points for the watchlist while noting marginal supply-chain risk for hardware-exposed Xiaomi.
